recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Revisit only if FHIR-I reopens the current standards status of CapabilityStatement.rest.security or revises the SearchParameter normative-status policy.
issue_request: FHIR-17175 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-I request to mark CapabilityStatement's security-service search parameter trial-use because the security backbone was trial-use; the Jira resolution agreed and noted tooling limitations for search-parameter TU marking.
initial_application: No FHIR-17175-tagged Git commit exists in the post-SVN history, but Jira records SVN revision 14528. The imported Git source in c69d71aa21/33b409a4b6 shows CapabilityStatement.rest.security and CapabilityStatement-security-service carrying trial-use standards-status, confirming the SVN-era request was applied.
additional_context: CapabilityStatement is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current search-parameter bundle marks CapabilityStatement-security-service normative. Later Published issue FHIR-25744 clarified that a SearchParameter definition can be normative even when individual resource uses or targets are not, and its implementation commit changed this search parameter from trial-use to normative. Current CapabilityStatement.rest.security no longer has a trial-use override, and a 2026 Zulip discussion treats CapabilityStatement as normative since R4.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Restoring a trial-use status on the current search parameter would conflict with the later FHIR-25744 status policy and the current source status of CapabilityStatement.rest.security.
